subject: literature
passage: For weeks, Amaru carried his grandfather's wooden flute in his coat pocket without daring to play it. The instrument was older than the house, and the tiny birds carved along ______ side had been worn smooth by decades of fingers. When he finally raised it to his lips one evening, the first note came out thin and shaky, yet his grandfather, listening from the doorway, smiled.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The side belongs to "The instrument" (the flute), which is singular, not to the birds carved on it. A singular thing as owner needs the singular possessive pronoun "its," with no apostrophe.
explanation.A: Correct. "Its" is the singular possessive pronoun, showing that the side belongs to the instrument.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Their" is plural and seems to refer to "birds," but the birds are carved along the side of the instrument, which is singular.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "It's" means "it is" or "it has"; "along it is side" makes no sense.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "They're" means "they are" and is plural; "along they are side" makes no sense.
